messages.text: ​​​​​Russell wins Dutch Sprint to trim title gap to Antonelli

metadata.summary: George Russell won the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint to maintain his perfect start to Formula 1's return to action and trim his championship deficit to Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli.
metadata.content: Dutch GP Sprint: George Russell wins from Charles Leclerc to trim F1 world championship deficit to Kimi Antonelli at Zandvoort | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Dutch GP Sprint: George Russell wins from Charles Leclerc to trim F1 world championship deficit to Kimi Antonelli at Zandvoort George Russell cuts his title deficit to Kimi Antonelli to 56 points with Zandvoort Sprint win; Charles Leclerc passes Lando Norris for second; Lewis Hamilton seventh; watch Qualifying later on at 3pm with Sunday's Dutch Grand Prix at 2pm, live on Sky Sports F1 Saturday 22 August 2026 12:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix Sprint race. George Russell won the Dutch Grand Prix Sprint to maintain his perfect start to Formula 1's return to action and trim his championship deficit to Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli. The polesitting Russell held the lead from Lando Norris at the start and and withstood an initial challenge from his fellow Briton before the McLaren fell into the clutches of Charles Leclerc's Ferrari behind. Despite being on the more brittle soft tyres compared to the mediums of those around him, Leclerc overtook Norris for second with an impressive move into the first corner on lap 18 of the short-form contest. messages.text: Antonelli to take Monza grid penalty for engine change

metadata.summary: World championship leader Kimi Antonelli will take a grid penalty at the upcoming Italian Grand Prix, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has confirmed.
metadata.content: Kimi Antonelli to take grid penalty at Italian GP in Monza for engine change, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff confirms | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Exclusive Kimi Antonelli to take grid penalty at Italian GP in Monza for engine change, Mercedes boss Toto Wolff confirms Kimi Antonelli to incur grid penalty for exceeding engine parts at Italian GP; championship leader to face at least 10-place penalty at home race in Monza; watch the Dutch Grand Prix on Sunday at 2pm (build-up from 12.30pm), live on Sky Sports F1 Saturday 22 August 2026 14:23, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli suffered a race-ending engine failure in Barcelona World championship leader Kimi Antonelli will take a grid penalty at the upcoming Italian Grand Prix, Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has confirmed. Each driver is permitted a capped amount of various power unit parts for the season, and two separate technical issues for Antonelli have left Mercedes resigned to the fact the Italian will need to exceed the limit before the end of the campaign. If possible, teams will generally choose to incur grid penalties at tracks where overtaking is easier, which is why Mercedes are set to install a new power unit for Antonelli at his home race in Monza from September 4-6. metadata.content: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Chester, Lingfield and Newton Abbot feature live on Saturday | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to content Today on Sky Sports Racing: Chester, Lingfield and Newton Abbot feature live on Saturday In Saturday's feature race on Sky Sports Racing, Lazy Griff and By The Book clash in a fascinating renewal of the Listed Chester Stakes on the Roodee; we also have competitive action from Lingfield and Newton Abbot, live from 1.55pm Thursday 20 August 2026 18:47, UK Image: Chester features on Sky Sports Racing on Saturday We have a busy day's racing on Saturday with action from Chester, Lingfield and Newton Abbot, live on Sky Sports Racing... 2.40 Chester - Useful stayers Lazy Griff and By The Book headline The feature event of the afternoon is the Listed Chester Stakes where quality pair Lazy Griff and By The Book headline a field of eight. Charlie Johnston fields Lazy Griff who has shown a decent level of form this summer building on his reappearance to score with aplomb at Sandown and he must shoulder a three-pound penalty for that success. Only seventh in the Goodwood Cup last month, he will need to return to his best if he is to land this prize. By The Book is a big danger for Charlie Appleby and Billy Loughnane.
